newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Rao seeks bail in forgery, bribery cases.
newsitem.headline: India's Rao seeks bail in forgery, bribery cases.

text.p: The Delhi High Court on Thursday opened a hearing into a bail plea by former Indian prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao in a criminal forgery case.
News agencies said Rao's lawyers also filed a separate appeal in the court for preventive bail to protect him against arrest in a separate vote-buying case.

"As the Delhi High Court has given bail to number of persons accused of murder and even of corruption... Mr Rao should also be given bail," Rao's lawyer, R.K. Anand, told the court in opening remarks in the forgery case.
Rao is charged with conspiring in 1989 to defame V.P. Singh, a Congress defector who later became prime minister, by forging papers to make it appear Singh had an illegal bank account.
The former prime minister has been charged in the case along with his one-time Hindu guru Chandraswami and the guru's aide, K.N. Agarwal.

The Supreme Court on Thursday granted bail to Chandraswami and Agarwal, who are both being held in Delhi's Tihar Jail, in a 1983 cheating case but said they could still be held if charged in another case.
The two were charged along with Rao on Wednesday in the cheating case, in which they are accused of swindling an expatriate Indian businessman out of $100,000.
On Wednesday, a Delhi judge granted Rao indefinite bail in the cheating case.
In the vote-buying case, Rao is charged with bribing opposition deputies to vote against a 1993 motion of no-confidence in his government, which he ultimately won.
Rao, 75, is the first former or serving prime minister to face criminal charges in India. He resigned as prime minister in May after his Congress party was defeated in general elections.
The three charges each carry maximum penalties of between five and seven years in jail.
Rao was denied bail in the forgery case by Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Prem Kumar on Tuesday and given until November 13 to appeal to a higher court.
Court sources said legal arguments in the bail plea in the forgery case could be lengthy. The court adjourned on Thursday after hearing Anand's arguments in the case.
The Central Bureau of Investigation would reply to Anand's arguments on Friday, they said.
If denied bail, Rao can appeal to the Supreme Court. But if he is rebuffed by the Supreme Court, he would have to surrender to the lower court on or before November 13, legal experts said.
